clue.text: Shift at sea with Coastguard — be in good shape

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and disordered, so the letters around it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coastguard officer's spell of duty on the water keeps them physically fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'at sea' does the shuffling of SHIFT, COASTGUARD and BE, with 'with' a link. A butcher's dog was well fed, hence the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in robust health and peak physical condition.

clue.text: Most definitely not good for one

parts.note: ill means bad or not good, as in ill effects
say means for example, as does 'for one'

explanation.surface: A firm denial that something is any good for a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an emphatic agreement, meaning certainly or absolutely.

clue.text: Group liking British lager one's brewed round pub

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round, enclosing, the abbreviation for the pub
beer is brewed, and brewing works its ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: Someone fond of British lager has a pint brewed near the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges LAGER ONE'S, and 'round' puts that around PH.
explanation.definitionFit: The English-speaking nations form a bloc sharing language and cultural ties with Britain.

clue.text: Clara Peggotty's parrot

indicators.note: the possessive says the letters belong to, and sit within, the words Clara Peggotty

explanation.surface: A Dickens character, Clara Peggotty from David Copperfield, owns a talking bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive ''s' is the only signal that the letters are held in the name; 'parrot' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to mimic or copy someone, as a monkey is said to imitate.

clue.text: Voluptuary disturbed by satire

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is upset by being mocked in a satire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person devoted to luxury and sensual indulgence.

clue.text: Unsurpassed as chicken served in velouté sauce?

definitions.meaning: a chicken breast dish in a cream-based sauce, named in French cookery

explanation.surface: A cook boasts that a chicken dish in rich white sauce cannot be bettered.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means paramount, and also names a classic French chicken dish with sauce suprême.

clue.text: King in French wood: he's claimed to be 1 17 27

indicators.note: the letter for the king is placed in the French word for a wood

parts.note: bois is French for wood
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch in a French forest boasts of his fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, then UK Prime Minister, said he was 'fit as a butcher's dog' after recovering from Covid.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Prime Minister Johnson made exactly that claim about his own health in 2020.

clue.text: Eggs on desperado finally roped in

indicators.note: a thing roped in is caught and held, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of desperado

explanation.surface: A cowboy's lasso snares an outlaw, with eggs somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roped in' puts O (the end of 'desperado') inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eggs, or a mass of spawn, are known by this name.

clue.text: Foolish speech: beaten President absolutely losing head

parts.note: Donald Trump lost the 2020 US presidential election

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: very means completely or absolutely, as in the very same

explanation.surface: A defeated president's rambling words are plain nonsense, as he loses his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes V from VERY, leaving ERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpery is showy rubbish or nonsense, including empty talk.

clue.text: Misses boomerangs collection that's found next to mine

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the word for misses returns, reading backwards

parts.note: gals are girls or young women, misses
a heap is a pile or collection

explanation.surface: Someone misses with a boomerang throw while gathering things near a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' and 'boomerangs' read as a verb pair; Misses are young women, GALS, reversed to SLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoil from coal mining was piled into tips beside the pithead.

clue.text: Macaque needs bringing back to life outside hospital

indicators.note: the word for revival goes around the letter for hospital

parts.note: resus is short for resuscitation
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A monkey needs resuscitating outside a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus monkey is a species of Asian macaque, used in medical research.

clue.text: Temple walk perhaps in flat area

indicators.note: the word for walking is placed in the word for a flat

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
walking is one way to go, travel

explanation.surface: A visit to a temple, perhaps on foot, in a level region.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower is a Buddhist or Hindu sacred building of East Asia.

clue.text: Sign that is featured in classical art

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is appears within the Latin word for art

parts.note: ars is the Latin, classical, word for art
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A symbol that appears in ancient Greek or Roman art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: A street better in central Greece or Antipodean location?

indicators.note: the run of letters is placed in the middle of the word Greece
central picks the middle letters of Greece

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Is a better street in central Greece, or somewhere down under?
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' and 'in' do the placing; 'or' is a link. Despite the Eastern Cape of South Africa, this one is in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: This cape is the easternmost point of New Zealand's North Island.

clue.text: Senior ministers are employed to produce fine articles

parts.note: the cabinet is the body of senior government ministers
to work is to be employed

explanation.surface: Top politicians are hired to deliver good results.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled joinery produces furniture of high quality, crafted pieces.

clue.text: Brief outfits for special figures?

parts.note: to prime someone is to brief them in advance
numbers are outfits, as in a smart little number

explanation.surface: Short garments made for unusual body shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief outfits' reads as skimpy clothes, but 'Brief' is a verb. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Integers divisible only by themselves and one are a special class of figure.

clue.text: Brussels collecting money raised to form alliance

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters read upwards, backwards
the EU collects, enclosing, the word for money

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: The EU raises funds so that members can band together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' does the enclosing, and 'raised', in a down clue, turns the whole upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together as one, to combine in alliance.

clue.text: See 1
Fabulous paradise bird held in irrational belief

parts.note: super means fabulous, excellent

indicators.note: the bird is held inside the word for paradise

parts.note: Sion, a spelling of Zion, is the heavenly city
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird of paradise from a fable is the stuff of irrational belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous paradise bird' suggests a mythical creature, but 'Fabulous' stands alone; Sion is a spelling of Zion, the heavenly city. 'held in' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief in luck or omens without reason is the classic sense.

clue.text: Tees put down again in European destination

parts.note: Tees is the setter, who refers to himself as I
to reland is to land again, to touch down once more

explanation.surface: The setter lands a second time in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own pseudonym for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The island republic is a European country and a popular holiday spot.

clue.text: Old bit in gym and some games area

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class
a set in tennis is a group of games

explanation.surface: An old piece of equipment found in a gym and a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish coin was a unit of currency before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Programme dropped with Christmas broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is put out on air, heard, so the clue words are judged by their sound

parts.note: shed is dropped and Yule is Christmas

explanation.surface: A programme was axed alongside the Christmas TV listings.
explanation.walkthrough: The British pronunciation, starting 'shed', is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable or plan of events is a programme.

clue.text: Surprise result having advantage over Egyptian deity

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead or having the advantage
Set, or Seth, is the Egyptian god of chaos

explanation.surface: An unexpected sporting result as one side gets the edge over a god.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock win by an underdog in sport is commonly called this.

clue.text: One leaving whole sheep's heart in dish

indicators.note: the numeral leaves the word for whole

parts.note: entire means whole
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heart picks the middle letter of the word sheep

explanation.surface: A whole sheep's heart served up in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I from ENTIRE to give ENTRE, then E, the centre of SHEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A main course or a dish served between courses goes by this French name.

clue.text: See energy returning to feed Australian god

indicators.note: the reversed letters go into, feeding, the abbreviation for Australian

parts.note: Aus is the abbreviation for Australian

indicators.note: returning means the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An Australian deity needs his energy back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the see-plus-energy pair backwards to EOL, and 'to feed' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he is the keeper of the winds.

clue.text: Liberal loves convenience

parts.note: love in tennis scores is nil, so two loves are two O's

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician enjoys having things easy.
explanation.walkthrough: A public convenience is the British euphemism for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Convenience is a polite word for a toilet or lavatory.

clue.text: Ace new doctor gone mad provides steroid

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: something gone mad is wild and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brilliant new doctor who has lost his mind supplies steroids.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sex hormone such as testosterone is a steroid.

clue.text: See 1
Tips from Aldous equipped with drugs in mixture

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two end letters, here of Aldous

parts.note: sorted is slang for supplied with drugs

explanation.surface: Advice from Aldous Huxley, the writer who described taking mescaline, on mixing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of various sorts mixed together, a mixed selection.

clue.text: Fashion consultant initially going well, then looking pale

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of going

parts.note: OK means fine, well
wan means pale and sickly looking

explanation.surface: A style adviser is doing well at first, then turns pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Gok Wan is a British television stylist and presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: The presenter of How to Look Good Naked is a well-known stylist.
